html:
A flood that began in late September 1887, when the Yellow River broke through its dykes in Henan province in Qing China. It killed at least 900,000 people by drowning, starvation and disease, and perhaps far more, making it one of the deadliest natural disasters on record.

The Yellow River carries huge loads of silt, which settle and raise its bed, so for long stretches it flows above the plain, held in only by dykes. After heavy rains the river broke out near Zhengzhou and poured south across the flat farmland into the Huai River system, swamping thousands of villages and several cities.

Repair took over a year. The disaster came only a few years after the great famine of 1876 to 1879 in the north, and showed how stretched the Qing state had become. The river had already changed its course to the north in 1855. Its dykes were broken again on purpose in 1938.
